## Abstract

[FILLED — structural frame; the two data-bearing claims are sealed and anchored;
the headline sentence is gated]

The calibration of exposure uncertainty is the field's own declared open question:
the community benchmarks that adjudicate mutational-signature tools report point
estimates and fitting quality but do not audit whether the reported interval
estimates cover at their nominal level (paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-scan.qmd §2
E8 [M]-class records: the 12-tool fitting comparison of Medo et al.,
Nat Commun 2024, and the 13-tool attribution benchmark of Jiang et al.,
Brief Bioinform bbaf042 — both re-pinned at DOI pass, Appendix A/§9). msuiter
addresses this by making interval calibration *measurable and cheap*: an R package
with a two-tier Rust core whose numeric kernels are bit-reproducible by
construction, an isolated-process kernel boundary with a frozen, version-stamped
protocol, published RNG stream layouts, and a measurement-and-attestation regime
(single-authoritative-shot campaigns, sealed floor tables with epoch digests,
co-tenancy censuses, hardware-pinned rows, firing constructed controls) that lets
every speed and correctness claim in this paper resolve to committed witness bytes
(vignettes/articles/performance.qmd:3-9 zero-fabrication design;
paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-scan.qmd §3 item 2, the banked RB-10/P-1/G5
record).

## 1. Introduction

[FILLED]

1. **The field's record.** Tool papers in this domain land in the specialty tier
   (the reviewer-side publication table: paper/review-05-nature-editor.qmd §1 —
   Cell Genomics, Genome Biology, PLoS CB, Brief Bioinform, Nat Commun), and the
   two flagship community benchmarks — the 12-tool fitting comparison and the
   13-tool attribution benchmark (Appendix §9, re-pinned records) — adjudicate
   extraction/fit quality without verifying exposure-interval calibration. That
   omission is the entry point of this work and is stated here only as the
   benchmarks' own posture, never as our novelty claim (the novelty claim proper
   is gated, Abstract/Title).
2. **What msuiter is.** One workflow grammar —
   `ms_variants() |> ms_tally() |> ms_extract() |> ms_fit() |> ms_compare()` —
   over SBS, DBS, indel, CNV, SV and RNA-SBS modalities, with a registry-swappable
   engine platform and the default path set to the self-calibrated methods
   (DESCRIPTION `Collate`/roster; README.md:7 "the Seurat of mutational
   signatures" positioning; engine-registry doctrine D15/D16,
   vignettes/articles/architecture.qmd §3.4, §5). The concept-to-API map is the committed
   MSU-MAP (vignettes/articles/msu-map.qmd, one row per exported NAMESPACE function, each row
   carrying its paper pillar and its peer counterpart or a recorded NONE reason).
3. **The thesis sentence.** msuiter's originality is architectural and evidential
   rather than algorithmic: it is the mutational-signature stack whose kernel,
   randomness, and measurements are individually attestable bit-for-bit — and the
   calibration audits that this makes affordable are the ones the field's own
   benchmarks declared missing
   (paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-scan.qmd §3 one-sentence draft, cited
   as-is per lane law; its (a)-class labels were targeted-rescanned on 2026-11-10 and
   the verdicts are reified in the erratum
   paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-rescan.qmd — Claim 1 (a) with one
   named caveat (Xue 2025, abstract unverified), Claim 2 (b) with narrowed "first"
   phrasing, Claim 3 split (c)/(b) — superseding the parent's pending statuses per
   its integrity note 7; the erratum's lane-2 pass then resolved its own open
   conditions in paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-lane2.qmd —
   Xue 2025 is abstract-verified PARTIAL-OVERLAP (same domain, different method:
   Bayesian/bootstrap/OLS-CI, no conformal, no strata), and N-of-1-time /
   ClockShares remain unverified on ~10 backends, so no "first" wording prints
   for treatment/timing deconvolution without a community primary source).

## 2. Software overview

[FILLED — DRY law: this section cites the committed architecture corpus rather
than re-prosing it]

- **Two-tier Rust core.** Pure numeric kernels in `src/rust/engine` with
  `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, zero FFI, zero dependencies at the kernel tier;
  the FFI shell is the only `unsafe` surface; directionality
  `ffi -> catalog -> engine` is asserted by a committed link witness
  (`src/rust/engine/src/lib.rs:25-29` per the paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-scan.qmd E1 row;
  frozen dependency budget and MSRV pin in `src/rust/Cargo.toml`);
  per-call thread pools, the global rayon pool never used (FFI contract 6).
  Narrative authority: vignettes/articles/architecture.qmd §2, README.md "Design pillars".
- **Determinism by construction.** Thread-invariance `identical()` laws,
  fixed-order reductions, published RNG stream layout `MSURNGV1` over
  (replicate, rank, fold) with cross-toolchain golden tests
  (`src/rust/engine/src/rng.rs` docs; paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-scan.qmd §2 E4 [verdict (b)]).
- **Isolated-process kernel boundary.** The `msuiter-kernel` CLI wraps the
  *unmodified* engine kernels behind a frozen, version-stamped protocol-1 CSV
  contract with `%{:.17e}` bit-exact round-trip, one-time handshake, per-case
  receipt attestation, all-or-nothing batches, and an endpoints-trace production
  face (`src/rust/engine/src/bin/msuiter-kernel.rs` protocol docs:1-64;
  `R/kernel-pipeline.R` design laws 15-29; law families in
  tests/testthat/test-kernel-batch-bridge.R, test-kernel-trace-shape.R,
  tests/kernel_cli_protocol.rs).
- **Platform grammar.** Engine registry as *data, not a class explosion* with
  governance fields (`engine_version`, `contract_version`, `certified`);
  six-modality unified tally with two-tier bit-compat acceptance; refdb
  governance with the zero-COSMIC-numeric rule (D3) — authority:
  vignettes/articles/architecture.qmd §3.4/§5-§7, vignettes/articles/msu-map.qmd, vignettes/articles/capability-matrix.qmd.

Table 3 — the T-1 decomposition of the census breach (arithmetic over the
sealed floor table; no new timing, not a parity claim).

| factor | evidence (committed bytes) | geomean over 21 classes |
|---|---|---|
| K — R interpreter → certified kernel (same protocol, spawn transport) | `post_v3` / `post_v3_rust` twins, `_FLOOR_ANCHORS` | **2.602x bought** |
| T — spawn-per-fit → batch-bridge transport | `post_v3_rust` / `post_v3_rust_batch` twins | **1.435x bought** |
| W — protocol work volume (batch face vs yardstick) | `post_v3_rust_batch` / `sigprofiler` cells | **10.959x REMAINING** |

The three factors are log-additive and exact by construction —
breach_R ÷ K ÷ T ≡ W (40.9041 / 2.6016 / 1.4347 = 10.9589 at the
ledger's full precision; the table's 4-significant-figure roundings
reproduce W to ~0.04%) — an accounting identity, not a
model. Shape mix measures ≈ absent: every O5 cell is a 96×1 single-sample
extraction (`bench/g0/g0/sim.py::sample_cell` — one counts vector per
(arm, n, rep); the N axis scales mutation mass, never matrix geometry), and
both sides are flat in N (yardstick 0.346–0.423 s/rep from N=10² to 10⁶;
batch face 3.880–4.968 s/rep). The faces execute the documented-defaults
`bp_extract_signatures` chain — 4 ranks × 20 bootstraps × 50 runs = 4000
NMF fits per rep (the batch face's own "frozen 20x50x4" record,
`bench/m7/competitors/p6_arms.py:111-116`) — against the yardstick's single
NNLS assignment solve per rep. The census breach is therefore
**protocol-inherited work volume**: with K and T banked and the kernel-time
lever measured at <= 1.31x (review-06 §1a), the <=2x row is unreachable by
engine optimization. Decomposition record with the full per-class census:
`paper/devlog-2026-11-28-t1-o5-gap-decomposition.qmd`; the work-volume lane
and its three contract-scoped shelves:
`paper/devlog-2026-11-28-t3-work-volume-lane-scoping.qmd`.

[FILLED]
1. **Venue posture.** The G2 co-author gate was not reached; the GB/NC ceiling is
   actively accepted (vignettes/articles/roadmap.qmd:173-180; the editor review's probability
   table, paper/review-05-nature-editor.qmd §8). This draft carries that posture:
   it makes no Nature/Nature-Methods claim.
2. **No parity row.** The <=2x peer-parity gate is measured BREACH and stays out
   of every table (§3.3 gate CAMPAIGN-R); the quotable performance content is the
   sealed verdicts and the O5 census.
3. **Synthetic-only.** Every number in this paper derives from the frozen
   synthetic regime (4.1); real-data columns arrive only with the gated G0
   primary and cohort work.
4. **One host.** The headline kernel measurements are pinned-host,
   power-state-uncontrolled single sessions, self-declared as such
   (vignettes/articles/performance.qmd:111-130); campaign rows carry host/hw_profile pins so
   their machines are auditable from the tables alone.
5. **Ground-truth lineage.** CS-2's byte-exactness oracle pair is named by
   lineage: one face is the team's own prior package (CRAN sigminer 2.3.3
   lineage, labeled as such), the other an independent derivation read from
   the published Cortes-Castro 2020 classifier definitions alone
   (novelty-scan §4 R8 landed 2026-11-17,

   the two are cross-adjudicated byte-exact, their open conventions pinned
   by a named table (tests/testthat/helper-hrd-independent.R), and the R7
   scarHRD face rides as third-party observation — none fabricated.
6. **Negative-search caveats.** The (a)-class originality labels in the novelty
   scan rested on the scan's self-declared flaky-backends environment; the

   pass (paper/devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-lane2.qmd) then resolved

   2026-11-10T07:49:51Z), Claim 3 split — TSB/RTT reporting is (c) prior art
